anti_overlap: Does not review individual feature completeness or persona coverage (those are Track A concerns)
Does not evaluate sync script implementation quality (that is a code-review concern)
Focuses on state-consistency and conflict protocols, not on whether the right data is captured
decision_lens: Separation assurance — the system must prevent two actors from acting on conflicting pictures of the same reality; any ambiguity in who owns a fact is a near-miss waiting to happen.
distance_rationale: ATC coordinates many independent pilots using a shared radar picture, exactly as ideagui coordinates many autonomous agents using a shared database — but ATC operates in physical space with real-time hard deadlines, while ideagui operates in logical project-state space with softer temporal constraints.
expected_isomorphisms: The ATC pattern of 'one controller owns a sector at a time' maps to the ideagui need for a single canonical source per fact. The ATC handoff coordination call (outbound controller briefs inbound before transfer) maps directly to the agent session-handoff problem: without a defined protocol, the next agent starts blind.
focus: Shared spatial picture integrity — does every actor always read the same authoritative state, and are conflicts resolved before they cause divergence?
name: fd-atc-situation-picture
persona: Air-traffic controller reviewing a sector handoff package: trained to spot any gap between what the radar shows and what is actually filed, to catch missing coordination calls, and to flag when two aircraft have conflicting clearances that will become each other's problem 10 minutes out.
review_areas: Single-source-of-truth discipline: are there any facts that could plausibly be stored in two places (beads AND Notion both writable for the same field), creating a dual-source conflict?
Handoff protocol completeness: when an agent session ends and another begins on the same project, is there a defined, schema-enforced handoff artifact, or is continuity reliant on convention?
Conflict detection: if two agents act on the same initiative simultaneously, does the schema or protocol have any mechanism to surface the conflict before both write incompatible state?

Stale-picture hazard: the CUJs document `last_synced` as a staleness signal, but there is no defined maximum-acceptable-age (MAA) per fact type; without it, actors cannot know when the picture is too old to trust.
Read-path availability: the vision names `bd ready` as a canonical fallback when Notion access breaks; is this fallback equally available to agents (Hermes via API) or only to the human operator?

severity_examples.condition: If two Hermes instances query and act on the same Initiatives DB row without any lock or versioning, conflicting updates will silently overwrite each other — data loss with no audit trail.
severity_examples.scenario: No conflict-detection mechanism between concurrent agent writes

severity_examples.condition: Agents and operators will make decisions from stale data without knowing it; the staleness warning in operator-portfolio-scan.md says '>24h flag a warning' but no equivalent exists for agents, meaning the agent CUJ has no freshness guarantee.

The operator CUJ documents `bd ready` as a Notion-unavailability fallback, but the agent CUJ does not specify what Hermes does when the Notion API is unreachable — agent fleet has no equivalent degraded-mode protocol.

success_hints: Every writable field has exactly one canonical store; Notion fields derived from beads are marked read-only in schema
Session handoff is a schema-enforced artifact, not a social convention
Each row type documents its maximum-acceptable-age before callers should treat data as stale
task_context: Reviewing the foundation-layer design of a portfolio meta-registry: three Notion databases, one human operator, and a fleet of autonomous agents that all read from and sometimes write to this shared substrate.
